info.description:
# Travibe API

Welcome to the Travibe API — a simple REST API for authentication, user management, and account access.

## Quick Start

All API requests go to: **`/api/v1`**

For example: `https://travibe.com/api/v1/users`

## How to Authenticate

We use **token-based authentication**. Here's the flow:

1. **Sign up or log in** using the auth endpoints
2. **You'll get a token** in the response
3. **Add the token to your requests** in the `Authorization` header

```http
GET /api/v1/profile
Authorization: Bearer your_token_here
```

### Tokens

- Each device or app gets its own token
- Send a stable `device_name` with every auth request to label the session
- If you request a new token with the same `device_name`, you'll replace the old one
- Some endpoints (like changing your email) require a verified email address
- Tokens stay valid until you log out

## What You'll Get Back

### When it works

Successful responses contain your data wrapped in a `data` field:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "12345",
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "name": "John Doe"
  }
}
```

Some operations that do not return data (like deleting a conversation or a
message) return `200` with a `message` confirmation.

### When something's wrong

**Validation errors** (status `422`):

```json
{
  "message": "Validation failed",
  "errors": {
    "email": ["Email is required", "Email must be valid"]
  }
}
```

**Other errors** (like bad credentials, status `401`):

```json
{
  "message": "Unauthorized"
}
```

## Buddies

Buddies endpoints help a signed-in user find people to meet. Discovery is opt-in:

- A user appears only when `show_in_travel_buddy` is on and the profile is complete.
- The viewer never sees themselves.
- A block in either direction hides both users.
- `city` and `country_code` are the user's current location, not a precise position.

The list endpoints accept these filters:

- `gender[]`: `male` and/or `female`.
- `nationality[]`: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 nationality codes.
- `languages[]`: language slugs.
- `interests[]`: interest slugs.
- `travel_styles[]`: travel-style slugs.

Values within one filter are OR-ed. Different filters are AND-ed. Each filter
accepts at most 20 values.

`GET /buddies/search` matches the current city exactly, after trimming and case
folding. Text after the first comma is ignored, so `Bali, Indonesia` searches
for `Bali`. An optional `country_code` narrows the current country. Results
never include trip data. Trips and Travel Matches are not part of this API.

## Stories

Stories are 24-hour photo posts shown in the stories bar at the top of the feed.

- Upload the photo through the media endpoints first (`POST /media/presign`, a
  direct `PUT` to storage, then `POST /media/{media}/finalize`), then send its
  id in the `media_ids` array to `POST /stories` together with the overlay
  document.
- A story holds exactly one photo. The `media_ids` array must contain that one
  photo id. The overlay is an app-owned JSON document (positioned text,
  stickers and drawing) that the server stores and returns verbatim, so the
  client re-renders the finished layout. `elements` must be a JSON array (up to
  50 items); each item's shape belongs to the client. String values under
  `text` and `content` inside `type: text` elements are also read for
  `@username` mentions; no other element type is inspected.
- A user can have at most 10 active stories at a time. Expired stories do not
  count. Creating an eleventh active story returns `422` with a `stories`
  validation error; the top-level `message` repeats the reason.
- The stories bar returns one entry per author, each story carrying its single
  photo's `thumbnail_url`. The full photo and overlay come from
  `GET /stories/{story}`. Each author group carries up to 10 active stories.
  The bar is paginated by author group: `page` and `per_page` (1-100, default
  15).
- `visibility` is `public` or `followers`. `location_name` is an optional label
  the app supplies; there is no server-side place lookup.
- Stories expire 24 hours after posting and are then deleted. An expired or
  unknown story is `404`; a story you may not see (a block in either direction,
  or a followers-only story you do not follow) is `403`.
- Watching a story records a single view per viewer
  (`POST /stories/{story}/view`). Repeat views refresh the timestamp but do not
  increment the count, and only the author can list who watched
  (`GET /stories/{story}/viewers`). The viewers list omits users blocked in
  either direction.
- Liking a story follows the same shape as post likes: `POST /stories/{story}/like` and
  `DELETE /stories/{story}/like`. The count rides on the story payload
  (`likes_count`, plus the caller's `is_liked`); only the author can list who
  liked it (`GET /stories/{story}/likes`), and the viewers list marks each viewer
  with `has_liked`.
- Deleting a story is immediate and returns `200` with a `message`; stories have
  no restore.

## Mentions

Mentions are written as `@username` in post text, comment text, or a story's
`text` elements. The server stores up to 10 distinct mentions per item and
returns them in the `mentions` array of the post, comment or story detail
response. Each entry carries the lowercased `handle` exactly as written and the
`user` it resolves to.

- The client finds each `@handle` in the text case-insensitively, matches it to
  a `mentions` entry, and renders it as a link. Everything else stays plain
  text; there are no character offsets in the response.
- A mention grants no access. It never changes who can see a post, comment or
  story.
- A notification is sent only to a mentioned user who could already view the
  content under the normal visibility rules: any user for public content, a
  follower for followers-only content, and nobody for private content.
  Self-mentions are stored but never notified.
- A comment mention notification targets the comment itself: `target_type` is
  the comment and `target_id` is its id. Its `data` carries `post_id` and
  `comment_id`; open the post with `data.post_id`.
- A blocked or unknown handle is silently left as plain text. Publishing still
  succeeds, and no mention row or notification is created for that handle.
- Re-saving unchanged content does not re-notify mentioned users. Widening a
  post's visibility can notify users who could not view it before.

## Realtime Notifications

The REST notification endpoints are the source of truth. Polling stays the
fallback. The WebSocket channel only delivers updates faster while the app is in
the foreground; it is not a background push mechanism.

- **Transport:** Reverb, using the Pusher protocol. Use a Pusher-protocol client
  (for example `pusher-websocket` or a native Pusher SDK). Laravel Echo is not
  used.
- **Channels:** `private-users.{id}` carries notifications. `presence-conversations.{id}`
  carries the open chat. A user can subscribe only to their own user channel and
  to conversations they participate in. One WebSocket connection can hold both
  subscriptions.
- **Authorization:** `POST /api/v1/broadcasting/auth` with the bearer token,
  form fields `socket_id` and `channel_name`. `channel_name` is
  `private-users.{id}` or `presence-conversations.{id}`. The response is the
  Pusher authorization object; a presence channel also returns `channel_data`.
  Another user's channel, or a conversation you do not participate in, is `403`.
- **Events:**
  - `notification.created` — the `NotificationResource` fields plus
    `unread_count`. Sent for a new notification, and when an existing
    notification becomes unread again. A `type: message_received` event is a
    new chat message; its `data` carries `conversation_id`, `message_id`,
    `message_type`, `preview` and `is_request`.
  - Like notifications (`post_liked`, `story_liked`, `comment_liked`) target
    the liked item. Their `data` is empty except for a comment like, whose
    `data` carries `post_id` so the client can open the thread. Removing the
    like deletes the notification again.
  - `notification.read` — `notification_id` and `unread_count`.
  - `notifications.read_all` — `marked_count` and `unread_count` (always `0`).
  - `notifications.read_conversation` — `conversation_id`, `marked_count` and
    `unread_count`. Sent when reading a conversation clears its
    `message_received` notifications, so other devices can correct the badge.
  - `message.sent` — the full `MessageResource`. Sent on the conversation
    presence channel and on the sender's `private-users.{id}` channel so other
    sender devices stay in sync. The client appends a message only when its id
    is new.
  - `typing.updated` — `conversation_id`, `user_id` and `is_typing`, on the
    conversation presence channel. It is ephemeral and is not stored.
  - `messages.read` — `conversation_id`, `reader_id`, `last_read_message_id`
    and `read_at`, on the conversation presence channel. Sent when a read marks
    at least one incoming message. It is ephemeral and is not stored.
  - The conversation presence channel also emits the standard
    `pusher_internal:subscription_succeeded` member list and
    `pusher:member_added` / `pusher:member_removed` events. Use the members for
    the live online indicator.
- **Reconnect:** the socket does not replay missed events. After a reconnect,
  call `GET /api/v1/notifications` and read pages newest first until you reach
  the last notification id you already have. Then call
  `GET /api/v1/notifications/unread-count` to correct the badge. For the open
  chat, call `GET /api/v1/conversations/{conversation}/messages?updated_since=`
  with the highest `updated_at` you already have.

## Push Notifications

Push is a wake-up signal, not the source of truth. The notification row and the
REST endpoints stay authoritative; a push carries only the notification id,
type, target and current unread count so the app can open the right screen and
refresh. Register a device with `POST /api/v1/device-tokens` and remove it with
`DELETE /api/v1/device-tokens/{deviceToken}`. A device that signs in to another
account is reassigned to that account, and each account keeps at most ten device
tokens. The raw FCM token is never returned or logged.

Push permission is the device setting. `push_notifications_enabled` is the
account setting; when it is off the notification row is still written and no
push is sent.

Email delivery is outside this API. Chat uses the conversation presence channel;
notifications use the user channel.

## Chat

Chat is 1:1 only. There are no group threads. The app keeps one WebSocket
connection. The open chat subscribes to `presence-conversations.{id}`; the user
channel carries notifications. REST remains the source of truth for history,
sending, read state, and reconnect.

- **Inbox.** `GET /conversations` returns accepted conversations and pending
  requests the caller started, newest activity first. `GET
  /conversations/requests` returns only pending requests received from someone
  else. Both accept `search`, a prefix match on the other participant's name or
  username. Message bodies are never searched.
- **Starting a thread.** `POST /conversations` takes the other user's `user_id`.
  A new thread returns `201`; an existing pair returns `200`. The thread is
  accepted immediately when the recipient already follows the caller, and
  otherwise waits for `POST /conversations/{conversation}/accept`. A request the
  recipient declines is deleted permanently. The recipient does not see a thread
  in their lists until its first message arrives. If they start the same thread
  first, it becomes theirs and they can send straight away.
- **History and reconnect.** Fetch
  `GET /conversations/{conversation}/messages` once when the chat opens. After a
  reconnect or foreground, pass the highest `updated_at` you have as
  `updated_since`. That returns new messages and changes to older ones, including
  deleted placeholders, read ticks and replies whose quoted message was deleted,
  so replace any message whose id you already have. Timestamps have one-second precision and the filter is inclusive,
  so a message you already have may come back. Previewing a pending request or
  reading across a block sends the other user no delivery or read receipt; after
  accepting, call `POST /conversations/{conversation}/read` again to send it. `after_id` returns only newer
  messages and misses those changes, and the two cannot be combined. To scroll
  back, request later pages. New messages shift the pages, so an older page can
  repeat messages you already have; match them by id. While the
  chat is open, `message.sent` delivers new messages; the client does not poll.
  Fetching marks the other participant's messages as delivered.
- **Realtime.** `message.sent` arrives on `presence-conversations.{id}` with the
  full `MessageResource`. Append it when the message id is new. The same event
  goes to the sender's `private-users.{id}` channel for other sender devices.
  The open chat does not need a GET per message. The `message_received`
  notification still updates the inbox and badge.
- **Typing.** `POST /conversations/{conversation}/typing` with
  `is_typing: true|false` broadcasts `typing.updated` on the conversation
  presence channel. It is ephemeral and not stored. The recipient of a pending
  request cannot type until they accept; a block in either direction is `403`.
- **Presence.** `POST /presence/heartbeat` every 30-45 seconds marks the caller
  online and updates `last_seen_at`, at most once a minute; `DELETE /presence` and logout mark the
  caller offline. `GET /conversations` returns `other_user.is_online` and
  `other_user.last_seen_at` when the other user allows `show_active_status`.
  The conversation presence channel also reports live member joins and leaves.
  A presence member list always shows who is in the chat: `show_active_status`
  hides the REST fields, not the channel membership.
- **Notifications.** Sending a message creates a `message_received`
  notification for the recipient and broadcasts `notification.created` on
  `private-users.{id}` over Reverb. Its `data` carries `conversation_id`,
  `message_id`, `message_type`, `preview` and `is_request`. A muted thread
  sends no notification. A thread the recipient hid comes back on a new
  message from the other user, and that message notifies them. The row also
  dispatches one FCM wake-up push, subject to the same rules as every other
  notification: no push for a muted thread, and none when the account's
  `push_notifications_enabled` is off or no device tokens remain. Email is
  not used.
- **Unread and read state.** Sending increments only the recipient's
  `unread_count`; `POST /conversations/{conversation}/read` marks incoming
  messages read and delivered, resets the counter and moves
  `last_read_message_id`. When at
  least one incoming message becomes read, the endpoint broadcasts
  `messages.read` on the conversation presence channel. Apply the event only
  to your own messages at or below `last_read_message_id`. Reading also marks
  the thread's `message_received` notifications read, so the notification badge
  stays in step with the conversation. The message
  payload still carries `delivered_at` and `read_at`, so a closed chat, another
  device, or a reconnect gets the ticks from an `updated_since` fetch.
- **Deleting.** Deleting a message keeps a placeholder for both participants,
  releases its media and, if it was unread, lowers the recipient's
  `unread_count`. Deleting a conversation hides it only for the caller and marks
  its `message_received` notifications read;
  when both participants hide it, the thread and its content are removed. While
  the thread still exists, a new message restores it for both participants.
  `POST /conversations` restores only the caller's own hidden thread.
- **Blocking and reporting.** A block does not delete the thread. It stays
  visible with `is_blocked: true` and sending returns `403`. While blocked,
  neither user sees the other's `is_online` or `last_seen_at`, and subscribing to
  `presence-conversations.{id}` returns `403`, so do not open that channel when
  `is_blocked` is true. The recipient of a pending request also gets `403` until
  they accept it, so previewing a request never shows up as a member join. A subscription that was already open stays open until
  the client disconnects. Report a user through `POST /reports` with `type=user`; chat has no separate report endpoint.
- **Media.** Send text, image, voice or video. Upload and finalize the file
  first, then pass its id as `media_id` with the matching message `type`. Images
  and voice clips are limited to 20 MB; videos to 100 MB. A video may also carry
  a poster image in `poster_media_id`. Audio and video can only be sent in chat;
  posts, comments, stories and avatars accept images only.

## Limits & Pagination

- **Rate limiting:** You can make a reasonable number of requests per minute. If you hit the limit, you'll get a `429` status.
- **Offset pagination:** Most list endpoints accept `page` and `per_page` (1-100, default 15):
  ```
  GET /api/v1/users?page=2&per_page=20
  ```
- **Cursor pagination:** Feeds, posts, comment lists, liker lists and
  notifications are keyset-paginated. Send `per_page` and, for later pages,
  the opaque `cursor` from `meta.next_cursor` (or `meta.prev_cursor`):
  ```
  GET /api/v1/feed/following?per_page=20&cursor=...
  ```
  These endpoints reject `page` with `422`. Their `meta` contains
  `next_cursor`, `prev_cursor`, `per_page` and `path`, and `links.next` /
  `links.prev` contain the complete URL. There is no `total` because a keyset
  page does not count the remaining rows.

get.description:
Returns public profiles only, most recent like first, each with follower
and following counts and whether the viewer follows them. Users in a
block relationship with the viewer are omitted. The parent post's
`visibility` must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.

The list is keyset-paginated: pass `meta.next_cursor` back as `cursor`.
`page` is not accepted.

A bearer token is optional; sending an invalid or expired one returns
`401`.
get.summary: List the users who liked a comment

Omit it for the first page.

Returns the resulting like state and the comment's updated like count.
Idempotent, and rejected with `422` for content from a user in a block
relationship. The parent post's `visibility` must allow the viewer,
otherwise `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

Returns the resulting like state and the comment's updated like count.
Idempotent: unliking a comment that is not liked is a no-op. The parent
post's `visibility` must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

post.description:
Returns the resulting like state and the post's updated like count so
the client never has to refetch the post. Idempotent: liking an
already-liked post returns `is_liked: true` with the same count and does
not create a duplicate. Liking content from a user in a block
relationship — in either direction — is a `422`. A new like creates an
in-app notification for the post author unless the liker is the author or
either party is blocked.

The post's `visibility` must allow the viewer, otherwise `403`.
Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

delete.description:
Returns the resulting like state and the post's updated like count.
Idempotent: unliking a post that is not liked is a no-op. The post-like
notification is removed. The post's `visibility` must allow the viewer,
otherwise `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
delete.summary: Remove your like from a post

get.description:
Returns public profiles only, most recent like first, each carrying
follower and following counts and whether the author follows them. Users
in a block relationship with the author are omitted. Only the story's
author may read the list; anyone else gets `403`.

The list is keyset-paginated: pass `meta.next_cursor` back as `cursor`.
`page` is not accepted.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: List the users who liked a story

Omit it for the first page.

post.description:
Idempotent: liking twice keeps the same state and does not inflate the
counter. The story's visibility must allow the caller, otherwise `403`;
an expired or unknown story returns `404`. A block relationship in either
direction makes the story unviewable, so it also returns `403`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

delete.description:
Idempotent: unliking a story that was never liked is a no-op and does not
change the counter. The story's visibility must allow the caller,
otherwise `403`. The story is hard-deleted at expiry, so an expired or
unknown id returns `404`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
delete.summary: Remove the caller's like from a story

post.description:
Authenticates the account and returns a bearer access token scoped to the
supplied `device_name`. Requesting a token for an existing `device_name`
replaces that device's previous token, so each device keeps a single active session.
post.summary: Sign in with an email address and password

post.description:
Creates a new account and returns an access token. The token is restricted
until the account's email address is verified, and a verification email is
sent. Verify the email before calling endpoints that require a verified account.
post.summary: Create an account and start a device session

get.description:
Returns the profile of the authenticated user. Requires a bearer token
with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: Get the authenticated user

post.description:
Revokes only the bearer token used for this request. Other device sessions
for the account remain active.

Returns the blocked user's public profile with refreshed follower and
following counts and `is_blocked: true`. Blocking yourself is a `422`.
Idempotent: blocking an already-blocked user returns `200` with the same
body and creates no duplicate.

A block is symmetric for interactions: after it, the pair can no longer
follow, like, comment on or save each other's content, and both
sides' posts are excluded from each other's feeds, profiles and saved
lists. Existing follows are left in place — unblock, then unfollow, to
clear both.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Returns the boolean plus the `user_id` it was computed for, which is
cheaper than paging through the blocked list when a screen only needs the
button state. This reports only your own block; a block by the other user
suppresses interaction too, but is not visible here.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: Check whether you have blocked a user

post.description:
Returns the user's public profile with refreshed follower and following
counts and `is_blocked: false`. Unblocking yourself is a `422`.
Idempotent: unblocking a user who is not blocked is a no-op.

Unblocking restores visibility both ways, but does not restore the
follows, likes and comments that were blocked while the block stood.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Returns public profiles, most recently blocked first, each with follower
and following counts and `is_following`, so the client can show whether an
unblock also needs an unfollow.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: List the users you have blocked

Signs the Pusher-protocol authorization response for one private or
presence channel. The authenticated user may authorize their own
`private-users.{id}` channel, or a `presence-conversations.{id}` channel
for a conversation they participate in. Another channel is `403`.

Send `socket_id` and `channel_name` form encoded, exactly as the
WebSocket server supplied them.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Returns capped previews for the two home sections plus the viewer's
profile-completion, visibility and current-city state, so the client can
choose between the completion card, the visibility promo and the
populated sections in one request. The viewer's own visibility does not
affect what they can see.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: Get the Buddies home screen

get.description:
Returns paginated `BuddyResource` items, ordered by shared-interest
count descending, then id. City matching is case-insensitive and
trimmed; when the viewer has a country code, candidates must share it.
A viewer with no current city gets an empty page with
`meta.has_current_city: false`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.
get.summary: List visible buddies in your current city

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

Matches users whose current city equals `city` after trimming and case
folding. A label such as `Bali, Indonesia` searches for `Bali`. When
`country_code` is present, the candidate's current country must match.
Results are ordered by shared-interest count descending, then id, and
never include trip data. This read never records a recent search.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

Returns at most ten rows, newest first. The cap is part of the contract,
so the response is not paginated.

post.description:
Upserts on the destination, ignoring case and whitespace, and refreshes

the comment or any reply beneath it are deleted with them.

The restored comment's reply and like counts are rebuilt from its active

notifications; each reply must be restored individually. Only the
comment's author may restore it; anyone else gets a `403`. A comment
that is not currently deleted returns `404`.

only the viewer's own counters change and the sender gets no receipt; read
again after accepting to send it. The thread's `message_received` notifications are marked read too,
which broadcasts `notifications.read_conversation` on `private-users.{id}`
when at least one changes. Returns the updated conversation header.

the thread is still a pending request or a block exists in either direction.
Non-participants get `404`.

Stores an FCM registration token for the authenticated account. The raw
token is never returned. Registering the same token again is idempotent
and refreshes its platform, because a device can sign in to another
account. The token then belongs to the current account. Only the ten most
recently used tokens per account are kept; older rows are deleted.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

A token that belongs to another account returns `404`, matching the

post.description:
Requires the account password, because the account email is what
password reset is sent to. Without this check, a stolen API token could
repoint the account at an address the attacker controls and then take the
account over through the reset flow — bypassing the `current_password`
that `PATCH /password` enforces. Verified before the code is generated,
so no mail is sent on an unproven request.

The code is only accepted by {@see self::verify()}; the account keeps its
current email until the new one is verified.

Address availability is checked *after* the password, not in the form
request. A validation rule would run first and answer 422 "email has
     * already been taken" for a registered address against 422 "password does
     * not match" for a free one, which tells a token holder which addresses
exist. Ordering it after the password means only a caller who already
proved ownership can learn anything.
post.summary: Send an OTP to the new email address (Figma "Email Address")

post.description:
On success the new address is marked verified immediately, since the
user just proved control of it.

Availability is checked before the code is redeemed, and reports the same
{@see OtpService::INVALID_CODE_MESSAGE} the code check itself would. A
registered address therefore looks exactly like an address with no valid
code pending, so this endpoint — which needs no password — cannot be used
to probe which addresses have accounts. That check and the write below
are separate statements, so an address claimed in the window between them
is caught from the unique index and reported the same way.

Other access tokens are revoked alongside the write: the account email is
the password-reset delivery address, so repointing it is a credential
change in exactly the sense {@see PasswordController}
treats a password change, and must evict other sessions the same way.

The address being vacated is purged of its own credential rows, for the
same reason `DELETE /account` purges them: reset tokens and OTP codes are
keyed by address, and a completed email change frees the old one exactly
as a deletion does. Leaving them behind hands whoever registers the old
address next a live reset token for their brand-new account. The purge
runs inside the transaction, and only after the code has been accepted,
so a failed verification purges nothing.
post.summary: Verify the OTP and switch the account to the new email address

post.description:
Marks the account verified and grants the caller's device token full
abilities when the token belongs to the verified account. A wrong or
expired code returns a 422 with one generic message, whether or not a
code is actually pending for the address. After five wrong attempts the
code is invalidated and a new one must be requested.
post.summary: Verify an email address with a 4-digit OTP code

post.description:
Public entry point for the "Didn't get OTP? Resend" flow. Throttling is
identity-blind: a 60-second cooldown and a 20-codes-per-day cap advance
whether or not the address has an account (or a verified one), so the
response never reveals account state. The echoed `email` is masked.

post.description:
The client uploads the bytes directly to object storage, then calls
finalize. Send `filename`, `content_type` (must be one of the allowed
image, audio or video MIME types) and `size`; a size over the configured
per-type maximum is a `422` here rather than at upload time.

Upload with the returned `upload_method` (`PUT`) to `upload_url`, sending
every header in `upload_headers` exactly as given — they are part of the
signature, and a mismatch is rejected by storage. The URL expires at
`expires_at` (10 minutes by default); after that, presign again.

The record starts at `status: pending`. The declared `content_type` is
not yet trusted — finalize verifies what actually landed in storage. After
finalize, pass the returned `media.id` to a post, comment, story or chat
message request to claim it. Leave `mediable_type` and `mediable_id` null:
media with a declared owner is treated as already attached and cannot be
claimed through `media_ids`.

No email verification required.
post.summary: Request a presigned upload URL and create a pending Media record

post.description:
Moves the record from `pending` to `processing` and queues the async job.
Images get derived sizes; audio and video become ready as uploaded. Poll
`GET /media/{media}` for `ready` or `failed`. A presigned URL is not
validation — the stored object is
measured and its real content type is sniffed, so an oversized or
unsupported upload is rejected with `422` and the record goes to `failed`.
An upload that never arrived is also a `422`. Calling finalize twice, or
racing two calls, gives `409` — only the first caller dispatches the job.

Only the media's owner may finalize it; anyone else gets a `403`.
If object storage cannot be reached, returns `503` and leaves the media
record unchanged so the client can retry. No email verification required.

record also carries an `error`, and `mediable_type`/`mediable_id` show
which post or comment the media has been claimed by.

Visible to the owner of the media and to any authenticated user for
ownerless records; anyone else gets a `403`. No email verification
required.

Fortify's `current_password:web` rule, which does not apply to
bearer-token (Sanctum) requests.

evicts sessions an attacker may hold (including ones registered by a
password reset). A bearer-token caller keeps the token that made the
change; see {@see RevokeOtherAccessTokens} for the session-authenticated
case.

The write and the revocation share one transaction. Committing the new
password while the delete fails would leave the caller with a 500, a
changed password they no longer know the current value of, and every
pre-existing token still valid — the exact state this endpoint exists to
prevent.

and returns `404`.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

`Cairo, EG`. This endpoint does not change `show_in_travel_buddy` — the

(`422`), and you cannot report yourself. One pending report per target
per reporter is allowed; filing a second one while the first is still

delete.description:
Requires the account password (see {@see DeleteAccountRequest}) so a
stolen token cannot destroy the account on its own. Revokes all access
tokens, purges the credential state keyed by email address, and
hard-deletes the user. The user's stories are deleted first so their
media rows and stored files are released; a plain row cascade does not
fire Spatie's media cleanup. The user's conversations are deleted through
the chat service for the same reason, so chat media is released instead
of surviving ownerless. The remaining related rows (posts, comments,
follows, likes, saves, hidden posts, blocks, social accounts) cascade;
media attached to those rows survives with a null owner.
Story view and like counters on other authors' stories are decremented
for the rows the cascade removes. Reference rows this user submitted — a
`languages` entry — also survive, with `created_by` nulled: cascading
them would take every other user's `user_language` pivot for that
language with it.

Notifications have no foreign key on the recipient's morph columns, so
the rows addressed to this user are deleted explicitly. Deleting the
user also removes notifications that target the user, the user's posts,
every comment on those posts, and the user's own comments together with
their reply subtrees. Notifications this user sent cascade through
`actor_id`.

The three writes share one transaction. The tokens and the
address-keyed credential rows are deleted before the user row; if the
final delete failed on its own, the account would survive with every
token revoked and its reset credentials purged, locking the owner out of
an account that still exists.

identity token must come from the provider's native or web sign-in flow.

follow, grouped by author. The caller's own group comes first, then
authors who have at least one unseen story — most recent unseen story
first — and finally authors whose stories the caller has all seen.
Authors in a block relationship with the caller are excluded in both
directions. Author groups are paginated with `page` and `per_page`
(1-100, default 15); each group carries up to 10 active stories. Only a
cover thumbnail and summary are returned here; the single photo and
overlay document come from `GET /stories/{story}` when a story is
opened.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

presigned and finalized; it becomes the story's photo. `visibility`
defaults to `public` and also accepts `followers` — stories have no
`private` option. `elements` is the editor's overlay document
(positioned text, stickers and drawing) and is stored as-is for viewers
to re-render; string values under `text` and `content` in `type: text`
elements are also read for `@username` mentions. A caller can have at
most 10 active stories at a time;
creating an eleventh returns `422` with a `stories` validation error; the
top-level `message` repeats the reason. The story expires 24 hours after

the caller has already seen it. A `followers` story is

and there is no restore. An expired or unknown story returns `404`.

view count; a repeat view only refreshes the view time and leaves the
count unchanged, so this is safe to call more than once. The story's
visibility and block rules apply (`403` when not viewable, `404` when
expired or unknown).

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

get.description:
Only the author can see who viewed their story; anyone else gets a
`403`. Viewers are ordered most recent first, and each row carries the
caller's follow relationship to that viewer so a Follow/Following button
can be rendered. Users blocked in either direction are omitted.

Requires a bearer token with full access and a verified email address.

the server stores and returns verbatim. Text elements are also
read for `@username` mentions: string values under `text` and
`content` in an element with `type: text` are parsed; no other
element type is inspected. Capped at
`config('stories.max_elements_per_story')` items and
`config('stories.max_elements_bytes')` encoded bytes.

UpdateLocationRequest.description:
Body for setting the caller's current location.

The client sends one string: the city and the ISO country code, separated by
a comma. The last comma separates the country code, so a city that contains
a comma still works, e.g. `Washington, D.C., US`.

location.description:
City and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, comma separated, e.g.
`Cairo, EG`. The country code is stored uppercase.

UpdatePostRequest.description:
Body for updating a post.

Every field is optional; omitted fields keep their current value.

media_ids.description:
IDs of images to add to the post. Audio and video are rejected.
Existing media is kept.

anyOf.description: Who can see the post. `public`, `followers` or `private`.

comments_disabled.description:
Whether new comments are rejected on this post. Existing
comments are kept either way.

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
General profile edit (`PATCH /profile`).

Accepts the same partial field set as the setup wizard, so it reuses the
wizard rules verbatim.

full_name.description:
The profile's display name. Max 255 characters. `name` is
accepted as a legacy alias.

username.description:
The `@`-less handle. 3-30 characters of letters, digits,
underscores or dots, starting and ending with a letter, digit or
underscore, and unique across accounts. Once set it cannot be
cleared; omit the key to keep the current username.

nationality_code.description:
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 nationality code, e.g. `EG`. Distinct from
`country_code` ("current country").

avatar_media_id.description:
The caller's own image to use as the avatar. Accepts media in
`ready` or `processing` status so the wizard need not wait for
async conversion. Send `null` to clear.

languages_spoken.description: Language slugs the user speaks. 1-4 entries; send `null` to clear.

items.description:
Active languages are available to everyone; a pending custom
submission can only be attached by the user who requested it.

interests.description: Interest slugs, e.g. `food`. 1-6 entries; send `null` to clear.

travel_styles.description: Travel style slugs, e.g. `budget`. 1-3 entries; send `null` to clear.

current_city.description: City-level current location, or null when it has not been set.

City and country code as one display string, e.g. `Cairo, EG`.
Null when the current city has not been set.

location_updated_at.description: When the current city was last set; null after it is cleared.

email.description:
Address availability is checked in the controller, before the code
is redeemed, and reports the same generic code error so this
password-free endpoint cannot be used to probe for accounts.
See EmailChangeController::verify().

determined by the endpoint, not by this payload.

email.description: The email address the code was sent to.
